edges.reason: Contextual understanding in this course setting depends on first understanding how language models process and represent language.
Maintaining interaction history is an advanced capability built on top of core language model behavior.
Answer generation relies on understanding the underlying language model that produces responses.
Evaluating the quality of language models requires first understanding what language models are and how they function.
Learning language models in a machine learning course generally requires prior understanding of how models are trained.
Modern language models are typically built on neural network foundations, so understanding neural networks is necessary before learning language models in depth.
Effective training depends on preparing, handling, and processing data appropriately beforehand.
Quality assessment is a specialized form of evaluating model performance and reliability, so general model evaluation comes first.
